To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutual funds and ETF sponsors have a fiduciary duty to their investors, but they are not currently fulfilling this obligation with respect to their securities lending programs.

mutual funds and ETF sponsors should: (1) disclose the full details of their securities-lending activities to their investors; (2) return to investors the full profits from their securities-lending programs; and (3) adopt a policy of lending securities only to borrowers who have a high credit rating.

mutual funds and ETF sponsors should: 1) provide more detailed and timely information about securities lending activities to fund shareholders; 2) provide more detailed information to shareholders about the use of collateral and the risks associated with the collateral and securities lending activities; 3) return to shareholders all profits generated from securities lending activities; and 4) disclose to shareholders the amount of time it takes to return collateral to fund shareholders.
